summary_plain: SAFFIRE-III burned large composite fabric samples inside an uncrewed resupply vehicle after it departed from the International Space Station. The investigation studied how rapidly large-scale fires grow in microgravity and how low-gravity flammability limits compare to normal-gravity tests. Understanding these fire behaviors helps improve fire safety for future crewed spacecraft and enclosed environments on Earth.
summary_expert: SAFFIRE-III (PSI-100) investigated large-scale fire growth and microgravity flammability limits using SIBAL solid fuel samples measuring 94 by 40.6 cm. Two tests were conducted inside the Cygnus resupply vehicle post-deberthing from the ISS at a forced air flow speed of 30 cm/s, varying the flow direction between concurrent and opposed. Diagnostics captured flame images, flow, flame, and plume temperatures, flame radiation, pressure, CO2 and O2 mole fractions, and flow velocity. The provided documents describe the objectives, design, and experimental setup for these tests.

key_findings.text: The Saffire-III experiments were performed on the Orbital Science's Cygnus resupply vehicle after it deberthed from the ISS, using SIBAL as the sample material at a flow velocity of 30 cm/s with concurrent or opposed flow.

The sample material used for Saffire-III is a composite fabric consisting of cotton on a fiberglass substrate (75% cotton, 25% fiberglass by weight) called SIBAL cloth, approximately 0.94 meters long and 0.4 meters wide.
